newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-PHILLIES HURLER HARRIS SUSPENDED FOR THROWING AT BATTER.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-PHILLIES HURLER HARRIS SUSPENDED FOR THROWING AT BATTER.

text.p: Philadelphia Phillies reliever Reggie Harris was suspended five games on Wednesday and fined an undisclosed amount by the National League for intentionally throwing at a batter Sunday against Atlanta.
The Players Association appealed on behalf of Harris and he will continue pitching until a hearing is held.

Harris was ejected from Sunday's 12-5 loss after hitting Braves outfielder Andruw Jones with a pitch in the stomach in the sixth inning. The inning before, Atlanta starter Greg Maddux nicked the bill of Phillies third baseman Scott Rolen's batting helmet, prompting a response from Harris.

"I'm not going to sit back and watch guys throwing at our guys," Harris said after the game. "I don't know if he did it on purpose, but it looked like it to me. I'm not out there to hurt someone, but I'm going to protect my teammates."
Harris was the losing pitcher in Wednesday's 7-5 setback to the visiting Florida Marlins, falling to 0-3 with a 5.20 ERA in 33 relief appearances this season.
